(Currently Amended) A method for controlling a flow of air, the method comprising: establishing a level of vacuum in a booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device using a pump; determining whether the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value; and terminating the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached the predetermined value, wherein said terminating the flow of air from the booster device includes closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device.

(Currently Amended) The method of claim 2, wherein said terminating the flow of air is accomplished via a directional control valve, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced, and wherein said pressure differential is at least temporarily maintained below a maximum threshold.

(Currently Amended) The method of claim 3, wherein said terminating the flow of air includes changing the direction of the flow of air and closing a flow path between the pump and the booster device, wherein said directional control valve is configured to facilitate said closing.

(Currently Amended) The method of claim 4, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, wherein said changing and opening are coordinated via the directional control valve.

(Currently Amended) The method of claim 5, wherein said changing the direction of the flow of air includes opening a path for a flow of air between the pump and the atmosphere, wherein said open path is controlled by the directional control valve.

(Currently Amended) The method of claim 6, further comprising filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump via a filter, wherein the filter is adapted to capture particulates.

(Currently Amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system, and wherein the system is optimized for efficiency in reducing pump load.

(Currently Amended) A system for controlling a flow of air, the system comprising: a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump is reduced while maintaining operation efficiency. 

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 8, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device, wherein this function is synchronized with the vacuum level.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 9, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump, wherein this action facilitates the reduction of suction pressure.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 11, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere, wherein this alteration is seamlessly integrated into the control strategy.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 12, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering a flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump, wherein the filter efficiency is integral to system optimization.

(Currently Amended) The system of claim 8, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for an automobile braking system, and wherein the system is designed to enhance braking responsiveness.

(Currently Amended) A motor vehicle comprising: an internal combustion engine; a booster device configured to provide a vacuum assist when a level of vacuum has been established in the device; and a system for controlling a flow of air from the booster device, the system including: a pump configured to establish the level of vacuum in the booster device by generating the flow of air from the booster device; and a directional control valve adapted to terminate the flow of air from the booster device when the level of vacuum in the booster device has reached a predetermined value, such that a pressure differential across the pump and a parasitic load on the engine are reduced, thereby enhancing overall vehicle performance.

(Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the directional control valve is further adapted to change the direction of the flow of air and close a flow path between the pump and the booster device, wherein the integrative control permits optimized engine efficiency.

(Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 15, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between a negative pressure chamber of the pump and a positive pressure chamber of the pump for improved operation.

(Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 17, wherein to change the direction of the flow of air the directional control valve opens a flow path between the pump and the atmosphere, wherein this enables effective disengagement of the vacuum.

(Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 18, further comprising a filter adapted for filtering the flow of air between the atmosphere and the pump to enhance system cleanliness and operational integrity.

(Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 14, further comprising a braking system, wherein the booster device is a vacuum servo booster for the braking system and configured to maximize braking efficacy.

(Currently Amended) The vehicle of claim 14, wherein the engine is a compression-ignition type optimized for performance and environmental compliance.
